title: Distance does not end a claim
literal_meaning: Even in the forest, the elephant belongs to the king.
explanation: The line presents a claim that persists despite distance. Applied figuratively, it can suggest that being out of sight does not by itself remove someone’s connection or responsibility.
meaning_odia: ଦୂରେ ରହିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ସମ୍ପର୍କ କିମ୍ବା ଦାବି ଶେଷ ହୁଏନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ଏହି କଥାକୁ ବୁଝାଯାଇପାରେ। ଏହା ଏଠାରେ ଏକ ସୀମିତ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା।
usage_example: Equipment lent to another office remains the lender’s responsibility to keep on its inventory. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: No source gloss accompanies the line. It is not used as evidence for any historical law giving a king ownership of all elephants.
